idiom_name: #if / #ifdef build flags plus a getenv()-driven feature struct
implementation_notes: Nothing in the standard library resembles a toggle router, so the full structure is hand-written: a struct of flags filled at start-up from getenv() or a configuration file, one named accessor per flag, and a plain if at the toggle point. Compile-time gating uses preprocessor conditional inclusion (#if / #ifdef), which removes the disabled branch from the binary entirely and is the right tool when the feature must not ship at all; runtime gating keeps both branches linked and switches on data. Because two threads may read the flag while one reloads it, the storage must be an object free from data races - _Atomic bool (C11, <stdatomic.h>) or a mutex-protected struct - otherwise a compiler may hoist the read out of a loop. A hand-written router is still justified when the decision has context (tenant, percentage bucket), because then the flat boolean is simply not the answer.
pitfalls: getenv() returns a pointer into the environment list; a later setenv() may invalidate it, so copy the value at load time instead of holding the pointer.
A plain bool written by one thread and read by another is a data race: use _Atomic bool (C11) or the flag may be cached in a register and the flip never observed.
Each #if combination is a separate binary: a build-time flag that CI never compiles rots silently, and the same #define name in two headers makes the effective configuration unreadable.
